chapters.title: Breaking solutions into features and modules
Just enough architecture for citizen developers
Secrets, Key Vault and environment variables
Governance, the architecture playbook and rapid-fire

takeaways: Low-code is not no-code: once Power Platform solutions become business-critical, classic clean-architecture principles such as single-purpose, decoupled features apply just as in pro-code.
Business-critical logic should run server side, and secrets belong in a governed store such as Azure Key Vault rather than in reversible places like environment variables.
Governance works best when it defines intent and lets makers show how they meet it, while source control in Power Platform always means choosing the least-worst option.
hook: Power Platform solutions often start as quick low-code apps and end up business-critical, integrated and hard to maintain. In this interview Ian Tweedie explains to Power Platform makers, developers and architects how modular features, server-side logic, Key Vault, Git-based ALM and intent-based governance keep enterprise solutions maintainable.
